name: pydantic-models-python
description: Define Pydantic validation models in models.py for application functions. MANDATORY separation of validation models from business logic.
role: Expert Python developer for data validation models. Enforce Pydantic BaseModel patterns with complete type safety and validation constraints.

file_structure.purpose: centralized location for all Pydantic validation models
file_structure.organization: group related models together, ordered by dependency (nested models first)

required: from typing import List, Dict, Any, Optional
optional: from typing import Union (if needed for complex types)
from pydantic import validator (for custom validation)

constraints.field_order: logical grouping - required fields first, optional fields last

    """Single item in an order with quantity and price."""
    quantity: int = Field(..., ge=1)

nested_models.pattern: define simple models first, then compose them into complex models

    """Single item in an order."""
    quantity: int = Field(..., ge=1)

    """Complete order data structure."""
    items: List[OrderItem] = Field(..., min_items=1)

forbidden_constructs: defining models in application function files
validation logic in models (use application function Err flags instead)
function parameter Field() definitions (those go inline in function parameters, not in models.py)
required_constructs: Field(...) for required fields with constraints
validation constraints (ge, le, min_length, etc.) where appropriate

best_practices.ordering: define nested models before parent models that use them
best_practices.granularity: create separate models for distinct concepts, even if similar
best_practices.reusability: design models to be reusable across multiple functions
best_practices.documentation: comprehensive docstrings help users understand data structures
best_practices.constraints: add all validation constraints in Field() - let Pydantic do the work
best_practices.simplicity: keep models focused on structure and validation, not business logic

complete_example.description: Complete models.py file with multiple models
complete_example.code:
from typing import List
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field

# =========================
# Pydantic validation models
# =========================

class OrderItem(BaseModel):
    """Single item in an order with quantity and price validation."""
    quantity: int = Field(..., ge=1, le=1000)
    price: float = Field(..., ge=0)
    product_id: str = Field(..., min_length=1, max_length=50)
    description: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=200)

class OrderData(BaseModel):
    """Complete order data structure with items and shipping information.
    
    Used by order processing application functions.
    Validates minimum order requirements and address format.
    """
    items: List[OrderItem] = Field(..., min_items=1, max_items=100)
    shipping_address: str = Field(..., min_length=10, max_length=500)
    notes: str | None = Field(default=None, max_length=1000)

class UserProfile(BaseModel):
    """User profile information with validated constraints."""
    user_id: int = Field(..., ge=1)
    username: str = Field(..., min_length=3, max_length=50)
    email: str = Field(..., regex=r'^[\w\.-]+@[\w\.-]+\.\w+$')
    age: int | None = Field(default=None, ge=0, le=150)

summary: all Pydantic BaseModel CLASSES in single models.py file
type hints required on all fields
Field(...) for required model fields (in BaseModel classes)
comprehensive validation constraints (ge, le, min_length, etc.)
define nested models before parent models
no business logic in models - only structure and validation
models are reusable across multiple application functions
IMPORTANT: function parameter Field() constraints go inline in functions, NOT in models.py
